newsitem.title: TURKEY: FORECAST - Turkish Feb CPI seen at 4.5-5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Turkish Feb CPI seen at 4.5-5.5 pct.

text.p: Turkish consumer price inflation is expected to have risen 4.5-5.5 percent month-on-month in February, bankers and analysts said on Friday.
In January, consumer prices rose 5.9 percent and wholesale prices climbed 5.6 percent from a month earlier.

"Alongside seasonal factors, fuel price hikes at the end of January and in February and the religious (Ramadan) holiday will have an impact," said Yarkin Cebeci, Garanti Yatirim Bank's assistant research director.
Cebeci forecast a 5.7 percent rise in wholesale prices and 5.5 percent rise in consumer prices. In February 1996, CPI was up 4.5 percent and WPI rose 5.8 percent.
By the summer monthly inflation will decline to 2.0-3.5 percent and in 1997 as a whole inflation will reach the government target of 75 percent if the current situation persists, Cebeci said.
Altug Karamenderes of ATA securities forecast a consumer price rise of 4.6 percent and a wholesale price rise of 6.1 percent in February.
An analyst at another brokerage said a monthly rise of 4.5-5.0 percent in February inflation was likely.
